core_obligations: Choose affine schemes V_i with a surjective etale V = coprod V_i -> Y and note that the topology on |Y| is the quotient topology of |V| (proof lines 6133-6136).
For each i choose an affine scheme U_i with a surjective etale morphism U_i -> V_i x_Y X and record that U_i -> V_i is surjective, flat and quasi-compact (proof lines 6137-6143).
Assemble U = coprod U_i and the square U -> X over V -> Y and verify that U -> V is surjective, quasi-compact and flat (proof lines 6144-6152).
Translate openness (resp. closedness) of T in |Y| and of f^{-1}(T) in |X| into the corresponding statements for the preimages in |V| and |U| and apply the scheme case (proof lines 6154-6159).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a flat, quasi-compact and surjective morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, a subset T of |Y| is open (resp. closed) if and only if its preimage in |X| is, i.e. f is universally submersive (source lines 6122-6130). The proof builds a square of presentations: an affine etale cover V = coprod V_i -> Y, then for each i an affine etale cover U_i -> V_i x_Y X, so that U -> V is the disjoint union of the surjective flat quasi-compact morphisms U_i -> V_i of affine schemes. The topology on |Y| is by definition the quotient topology of |V|, and the criterion for f reduces to the scheme case for U -> V, which is the fpqc quotient topology lemma.
